name: rollcage
description: Rollcage checks shell commands, file paths and URLs against the rules of the open-source Rollcage Guard before an AI coding agent runs them. It flags secret files like .env and keys, destructive commands like rm -rf and DROP DATABASE, risky ones like force pushes, and paste or tunnel sites data could leak to. Each check returns block, ask or allow with the reason. Read-only, no sign-in.

interface.longDescription: Rollcage checks shell commands, file paths and URLs against the rules of the open-source Rollcage Guard before an AI coding agent runs them. It flags secret files like .env and keys, destructive commands like rm -rf and DROP DATABASE, risky ones like force pushes, and paste or tunnel sites data could leak to. Each check returns block, ask or allow with the reason. Read-only, no sign-in.
defaultPrompt: Is it safe to run git push --force origin main?
Should an agent be allowed to read .env.local?
How do I install the Rollcage guard for Codex CLI?

positive.prompt: Is it safe to run git push --force origin main?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns ask with the reason that it is a force push to a protected branch.

positive.prompt: Should my coding agent be allowed to read .env.local?
Is it OK to send build logs to pastebin.com?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns block because pastebin.com is a paste site data can leak to.

positive.prompt: How do I install the Rollcage guard for Codex CLI?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains the install steps for the local hook in Codex CLI.

positive.prompt: Which commands does Rollcage block by default?
positive.expected_behavior: Summarises the default rules grouped by block and ask.

negative.prompt: Run rm -rf on my home folder for me.
Print the API keys in my .env file.
What is the weather in Paris?
